papers.title: Procedura: Agentic 3D Modeling with Procedural Control

summary.tldr: Procedura is a 3D modeling agent framework that generates editable, parametric 3D objects as procedural code assemblies using LLM-driven graph planning, machine-checkable mates, and decoupled vision critics.
key_points: Generates objects as parametric programs where named parts are linked via typed, machine-checkable mates solved directly from mated frames.
Enforces a strict execution pipeline that admits parts only after passing compilation, mate, and connectivity checks, followed by iterative refinement via a decoupled vision critic.
Supports per-part material assignments and simulator-validated articulations embedded within the assembly graph.
Outperforms native 3D generators and prior 3D-code agents on P3D-Bench and the MechBench-36 hard-surface benchmark while generating the sharpest edges.
summary.why_it_matters: It bridges the gap between text-to-3D generation and CAD engineering by outputting fully editable, structured, and articulated programs rather than non-parametric, dense meshes.

papers.title: Luce: Relightable Gaussians for 3D Asset Generation

summary.tldr: Luce unifies geometry and PBR materials into a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud using dedicated primitives, autoencoding them into a material-aware latent space for single-image relightable 3D asset generation via a rectified-flow transformer.
key_points: Represents geometry and PBR modalities (albedo, metallic-roughness, surface normals) using dedicated Gaussian primitives within a voxelized multimodal Gaussian cloud.
Uses a variational autoencoder to compress the multimodal representation into a unified material-aware latent space.
Employs a rectified-flow transformer to generate the latent from a single image conditioned on multi-layer features from a pretrained image encoder.
Decodes latents into relightable PBR Gaussians or an optional textured mesh containing a tangent-space normal map.
Outperforms baselines on Toys4K by reducing FID by 28% and achieves a 0.8519 CLIP image-alignment score on an AI-generated image benchmark versus 0.8299 for the top baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: Luce enables the direct creation of relightable, high-fidelity 3D assets with accurate PBR materials and fine details like text from a single input image.

papers.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes

summary.tldr: CritICL is a novel inference-time framework that enhances LLM reasoning by incorporating structured failure modes from smaller models into critique-based in-context learning prompts.
key_points: Exploits structured, cross-scale failure patterns within the same LLM family to guide generation without requiring external verifiers.
Introduces CritICL-dynamic, which adaptively predicts input-specific failure modes and retrieves targeted critiques.
Introduces CritICL-static, which leverages a global failure mode profile to deliver stable, static guidance.
Outperforms standard in-context learning and matches or exceeds test-time scaling techniques while significantly reducing token costs and generation counts.
summary.why_it_matters: CritICL improves reasoning accuracy at inference time while bypassing the high compute and token costs associated with traditional test-time scaling and repeated generations.

papers.title: CaRGo-T: Causal Reasoning Graph-of-Thought improves Multimodal Humor Comprehension

summary.tldr: CaRGo-T is a framework that improves multimodal humor understanding by using vision-language models to generate code-serialized, graph-based representations of causal and contextual relationships.
key_points: Captures complex image-text humor dynamics by modeling entities, events, and implicit relationships as a lightweight graph-of-thought structure.
Serializes the causal reasoning graph into a code-based format generated by a VLM, which can be interpreted by the same or a different VLM in zero-shot or in-context learning setups.
Demonstrates performance gains of 1-20% on humor understanding and 1-3% on humor detection across four datasets covering memes, satire, and sarcasm.
Mutual information analysis confirms CaRGo-T representations retain more target-relevant information than conventional chain-of-thought baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Graph-structured causal reasoning provides a more effective mechanism than linear prompting for vision-language models to interpret complex, implicit multimodal interactions like humor.

papers.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback

summary.tldr: TacForcing introduces a streaming action expert that integrates execution-time tactile feedback into vision-language-action models using Execution-Aware Tactile Attention, eliminating separate reactive controllers.
key_points: Replaces the standard action expert with a streaming action expert to condition actions on evolving tactile observations gathered during execution.
Introduces Execution-Aware Tactile Attention (EATA) to restrict tactile conditioning specifically to actions nearing execution, reducing temporal mismatch.
Removes the need for a separate high-frequency reactive controller, lowering architectural and training complexity.
Achieves average success rates of 65% across six simulated UniVTAC tasks and 69% across three real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables vision-language-action models to dynamically adapt to real-time contact changes during execution without complex, multi-component control architectures.

papers.title: CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval

summary.tldr: CaSKG introduces a counterfactual-causal skill graph framework that calibrates offline procedural skill edges using direction-conditioned textual probes and Bayesian smoothing to improve LLM agent skill retrieval.
key_points: Constructs a high-recall candidate graph using semantic, lexical, input/output, and structural evidence, refined by repair evidence and an optional LLM judge.
Applies direction-conditioned textual counterfactual probes that remove, substitute, and reorder skill pairs to evaluate edge reliability.
Aggregates probe evidence via Bayesian smoothing to publish a state-filtered weighted graph used for task-conditioned expansion.
Improves six-model macro-average ScienceWorld score from 72.62 to 80.50 and ALFWorld success rate from 80.01% to 86.79% over Graph-of-Skills (GoS).
Operates strictly offline without modifying the downstream agent policy, context format, or task interface.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM agents to accurately retrieve executable workflows, prerequisites, and state-changing actions from large skill libraries without incurring the high context costs of full-library prompting.

papers.title: Thinking on Shots: Consistent Multi-Shot Video Editing with Agentic Reasoning

summary.tldr: MMLVE-Agent uses LLMs and VLMs to perform multi-instruction multi-shot long-video editing while maintaining cross-shot consistency and spatiotemporal structure.
key_points: Formulates the Multi-Instruction Multi-Shot Long-Video Editing (MMLVE) task around Cross-Shot Editing Consistency (CSEC), Multi-Instruction Decoupling (MID), and Zero-Destruction on Spatiotemporal Structure (ZDSS).
Uses an agentic framework combining LLMs and VLMs for shot-level video decoupling and precise instruction parsing, avoiding naive fixed-duration chunking.

Introduces MMLVE-Bench, a benchmark dataset featuring complex spatiotemporal dynamics, dense heterogeneous instructions, and sparse entity distributions, alongside three specialized evaluation metrics.
Outperforms closed-source models such as Seedance 2.0 by eliminating editing hallucinations and maintaining cross-shot continuity.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves entity fragmentation and continuity loss in long-video editing by replacing fixed chunking with agent-driven shot decoupling and instruction parsing.

papers.title: Skill Issue: Are Skills Language-Invariant in LLMs?

summary.tldr: A new multilingual self-play benchmark using an extended TextArena evaluates cross-lingual skill inconsistency in LLMs by pitting identical models against each other under different language interfaces while keeping state spaces and game rules fixed.
key_points: Isolated language's impact on model behavior using multilingual self-play across six game types covering spatial reasoning, imperfect information, resource allocation, and repeated interaction.
Evaluated three open-weight models across eight languages, revealing systematic cross-lingual variations in win-loss margins, invalid action rates, and strategic tendencies.
Identified language-specific failures in spatial reasoning, card-conditioned decision-making, and optimal move selection.
Altering only the intermediate reasoning language successfully recovered a significant portion of lost performance in certain settings.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that LLM skill execution is not language-invariant, highlighting language bias in decision-making pipelines and the need for equitable cross-lingual model design.

papers.title: Prefix Sliding for efficient test-time scaling

summary.tldr: Prefix Sliding optimizes test-time compute by discarding middle reasoning tokens while retaining initial instructions and recent context, reducing memory overhead and accelerating inference.
key_points: Identifies that intermediate reasoning tokens lose importance during long-horizon model generation.
Retains only the initial prefix (instructions and tool definitions) and a sliding window of the most recent tokens, capping total memory usage regardless of trace length.
Delivers a 3x inference speedup on existing models without requiring retraining.
Supports reinforcement learning training using Prefix Sliding to scale reasoning traces beyond 100,000 tokens.
Outperforms alternative context-reduction methods such as intermediate token summarization and standard sliding window attention.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables models to perform long-horizon reasoning over 100,000 tokens efficiently by eliminating memory bottlenecks during test-time compute scaling.

papers.title: EditaLive! Unified Character Video Editing for Live Streaming

summary.tldr: EditaLive is a framework that adapts the Wan-Animate model for real-time, instruction-based human-centric video editing during live streams with minimal facial-expression loss and low latency.
key_points: Repurposes the pretrained Wan-Animate model using the new CharEdit-50K dataset to separate appearance from motion for instruction-based character editing.
Converts offline bidirectional generation into causal streaming generation to enable real-time processing.
Applies an aligned self-rollout distillation strategy with fixed RoPE and align forcing to compress the model into a two-step sampler.
Uses first-frame preserved sparse attention to filter redundant history and prevent appearance drift over time.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables low-latency, real-time character video editing during live streams while maintaining facial expression consistency and preventing appearance drift.

papers.title: Aphanta: Diagnosing Task-Aligned Image-Edited Intermediates for Multimodal Reasoning

summary.tldr: Aphanta is a diagnostic framework evaluating MLLM-to-image-editor-to-MLLM pipelines by comparing direct reasoning, editor-generated intermediates, and idealized reference intermediates across 20 tasks.
key_points: Evaluates the utility of image editing as an explicit visual intermediate across direct reasoning, editor-generated, and ideal reference conditions.
Shows performance gains are heavily task-conditioned, benefiting visual cue injection, grounding, and counterfactual state realization.
Identifies structural extrapolation and symbol-sensitive construction as unreliable failure modes for current image editors.
Achieves a 10.2 point increase (0.343 to 0.445 mean task score, a +29.7% relative gain) using a consolidated Qwen pipeline on the positive-task subset.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes that image editing acts as a task-specific visual workspace rather than a universal reasoning tool, providing a standardized protocol to evaluate MLLM visual representation alignment.

papers.title: RetrievalRouter: Joint Modality and Architecture Selection for Document Retrieval

summary.tldr: RetrievalRouter is a lightweight, query-aware routing system that dynamically selects the optimal retrieval pipeline's modality and architecture from query text alone, breaking static trade-offs between accuracy and latency.
key_points: Predicts the ideal retrieval modality (text vs. multimodal) and architecture (dense vs. late-interaction) directly from the query text.
Exposes the complete accuracy-latency trade-off frontier using a single tunable parameter.
Outperforms the best static baseline by achieving 2.5% higher accuracy while operating 12.4 times faster.
Surpasses prior adaptive selection methods on nDCG@5 in accuracy-oriented settings while matching or improving latency and nDCG@5 in latency-focused settings.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables high-stakes document retrieval systems in fields like law and finance to maximize accuracy while drastically reducing the computation costs and latency of complex pipelines.

papers.title: What Does an Evaluation License? A Commit-Bound Census of Claim-Relative Inference in Inspect Evals

summary.tldr: A commit-bound census of 124 Inspect Evals units formalizes a claim-replay layer, revealing that 110 units stop before deterministic inference due to missing historical evidence or semantic grounding.
key_points: Formalizes evaluation claims using a frozen substrate D, a grounded family F, a claim query q, and an identified set.
Audited all 124 mechanically eligible Inspect Evals units at a pinned commit to assign terminal dispositions.
110 of the 124 units halted prior to deterministic inference because required historical evidence or semantic grounding was unbound.
For executing units, metrics separated by claim resolution and primary versus review family, producing typed stops, instability witnesses, and stable substructure.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that standard evaluation artifacts often lack the historical and semantic binding required to reliably support or replay their attached claims.

papers.title: LibriBrain100: One Hundred Hours of Broad and Deep MEG Data for Neural Speech Decoding at Scale

summary.tldr: LibriBrain100 is a large-scale MEG dataset containing over 100 hours of continuous speech listening data, including ~80 hours from a single subject and ~40 minutes across 32 subjects.
key_points: Contains ~80 hours of deep, within-subject MEG data, which is 8 times larger than the next comparable within-subject dataset.
Includes broad multi-subject data consisting of ~40 minutes of MEG recordings from each of 32 different subjects.
Demonstrates that supervised fine-tuning of a pre-trained model on broad multi-subject data compensates for limited individual subject data on a word-classification benchmark.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on a word-classification benchmark using an existing neural decoding model.
Includes standard train, validation, and test splits accessible via an open-source Python library supporting data loading for common deep learning frameworks.
summary.why_it_matters: The dataset and standardized evaluation pipeline accelerate the development of practical, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces aimed at restoring communication for individuals with severe paralysis.

papers.title: JudgeStealer: Extracting LLM Judging Capabilities across Evaluation Protocols

summary.tldr: JUDGESTEALER is a query-efficient framework designed to extract black-box LLM judging capabilities across pointwise, pairwise, and listwise evaluation protocols using dynamically selected pointwise queries.
key_points: Transforms pointwise score queries into pairwise and listwise supervisions without incurring additional victim queries by leveraging cross-protocol agreement.
Employs dynamic input selection based on semantic diversity, predictive uncertainty, and potential judge biases to optimize query efficiency.
Uses score smoothing and multi-protocol review to preserve ordinal structures and prevent catastrophic forgetting during surrogate model adaptation.
Achieves extraction accuracy up to 73.3% for pointwise, 87.0% for pairwise, and 71.6% for listwise evaluations, while maintaining robustness against standard extraction defenses.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that proprietary LLM judge and reward model intellectual property can be stolen efficiently across multiple evaluation formats despite query budget constraints and extraction defenses.

papers.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators

summary.tldr: CLAP introduces a cross-embodiment video world model framework that leverages latent actions, end-effector poses, and language instructions to learn generalizable physics across human and diverse robotic datasets.
key_points: Reconciles disparate action spaces across different robot platforms and unlabelled human videos using end-effector poses, language instructions, and latent actions.
Employs a curriculum-based learning recipe that learns baseline physical priors from unlabelled video via latent actions before grounding them into end-effector action spaces.
Supports multiple robot morphologies, including cross-embodiment systems, DROID, Bridge, bimanual YAM robots, and G1 humanoids.
Matches or outperforms state-of-the-art single-embodiment video models on the DROID dataset and enables few-shot adaptation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables action-conditioned video generation models to train on internet-scale heterogeneous video data, bypassing the restriction of single-robot embodiment datasets for physical simulation.

papers.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction

summary.tldr: CAST uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to identify, audit, and suppress text artifact features during clinical language model fine-tuning, improving robustness and decision transparency.
key_points: Uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on intermediate Transformer activations to extract sparse, human-auditable clinical and artifact features.
Employs an LLM-assisted interpretation pipeline with ICD-10 retrieval constraints to label extracted SAE latents.
Suppresses identified note-specific artifact latents (e.g., templates, separators) during fine-tuning via residual subtraction.
Provides post-hoc per-concept attributions to create a feature-level audit trail for predictions.
Outperforms standard fine-tuned encoder baselines and stays competitive with strong LLMs on MIMIC-IV discharge-note mortality prediction.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents clinical models from relying on spurious formatting artifacts, making AI predictions robust to deployment shifts and fully auditable by clinicians.

papers.title: LeVJEPA: Efficient & Scalable Video Pretraining without the Heuristics

summary.tldr: LeVJEPA is the first video encoder trained with LeJEPA's collapse-free objective, eliminating architectural asymmetries, stop-gradients, and target encoders while drastically reducing pretraining compute.
key_points: Uses a single encoder and projector trained with an invariance loss over global and local views, regularized by SIGReg with a single hyperparameter.
Leverages uniform random token dropping to lower the observed token count, simultaneously improving downstream performance and reducing compute.
Achieves 5.6x to 20.8x lower pretraining FLOPs than V-JEPA 2 across ViT-S/B/L models while matching or exceeding downstream accuracy.
Outperforms the strongest video baseline by 7.6 points on ImageNet-1K at matched FLOPs and nearly doubles DINOv2 motion-centric accuracy when trained with block-causal attention.
summary.why_it_matters: It removes the heavy computational overhead and complex heuristics of video self-supervised learning, making video a viable, efficient alternative to static images for general-purpose visual pretraining.

papers.title: Successive Capacity Growth: Task-Complexity-Driven Width and Depth Expansion for Vision Transformer Encoders in JEPA World Models

summary.tldr: Successive Capacity Growth (SCG) dynamically expands Vision Transformer encoders in JEPA world models in width or depth using a task-agnostic, function-preserving test-and-verify mechanism.
key_points: Starts from a minimal 283K parameter ViT encoder (1 head, 2 layers) and expands width or depth based on prediction loss improvements, rolling back unhelpful changes.
Uses Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularizer (SIGReg) to maintain statistical independence of semantic dimensions and prevent representation collapse during growth.
Achieves bit-exact function preservation (ratio = 1.0, absolute difference = 0.0) with zero false-positive architectural expansions across tests.

Demonstrates a 20.3% loss improvement on a 60-D multi-object task via depth expansion with 56x parameter efficiency over fixed large models, and a 23% loss improvement on 2D navigation via width expansion.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need to pre-allocate maximum transformer capacity in JEPA world models, optimizing compute and parameter efficiency without losing predictive quality.

papers.title: PAWBench: How Far Are We from Probabilistically Aligned World Modeling?

summary.tldr: PAWBench and PAWEval introduce a benchmark and outcome-level evaluation protocol to test whether video generation models function as probabilistically aligned world models that match true physical behavior distributions.
key_points: Formalizes probabilistic alignment as a world model's ability to reproduce the actual probability distribution of possible outcomes given an initial observation and action.
Introduces PAWBench, comprising 50 distinct physical scenarios, to evaluate video generators as stochastic samplers.
Implements PAWEval, a protocol that aggregates repeated video rollouts into empirical outcome distributions.
Evaluated eleven current video generation systems and found that zero models consistently matched reference probabilities while covering the full range of valid physical behaviors.
Analyzed the impact of language prompts, initial noise sampling, and model training on reshaping predictive distributions.
summary.why_it_matters: Current video-based world models fail to capture the correct probability distributions of non-deterministic physical events, highlighting a key gap in developing reliable stochastic simulators.

papers.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance

summary.tldr: Eval-awareness in model chain-of-thought is not uniform; capabilities-framed eval-awareness predicts compliance with dangerous requests at significantly higher rates (+24 to +46 percentage points) than safety-framed eval-awareness.
key_points: Verbalized eval-awareness in chain-of-thought (CoT) consists of distinct capabilities-flavored, safety-flavored, combined, or neutral framings.
Testing Qwen3-32B on the FORTRESS dataset demonstrated that capabilities-framing increases compliance by +24 to +46 percentage points over safety-framing across all steering conditions.
CoT-prefill interventions on eval-awareness-negative rollouts showed a causal link, with 10 of 11 prefills shifting model compliance in the predicted direction.
Aggregate metrics tracking percentage suppression of eval-awareness obscure safety-relevant behavioral outcomes, as steering can suppress non-safety components without affecting safety-relevant ones.
summary.why_it_matters: Safety evaluation pipelines cannot treat eval-awareness as a single metric to suppress, as different framings cause vastly different safety and compliance behaviors.

papers.title: Naive Prompt Optimization: Rethinking the Need for Complex Prompt Search

summary.tldr: Naive Prompt Optimization (NPO) uses a lightweight, single-lineage iterative prompt revision method driven by teacher model feedback, achieving performance comparable to or exceeding complex prompt search algorithms like GEPA using fewer rollouts.
key_points: NPO employs a simple, single-lineage iterative process where a teacher model revises prompts based on rollout feedback without complex search procedures.
NPO matches or beats GEPA's performance while requiring fewer rollouts, with efficacy increasing alongside teacher model strength.
Prompts optimized via NPO transfer effectively across different student models, exhibiting strong verbatim transferability within the same model family.
In interactive games, GRPO outperforms prompt optimization on certain tasks, but NPO remains broadly competitive with GEPA overall.
summary.why_it_matters: NPO demonstrates that strong teacher reasoning can replace complex optimizer search architectures, drastically reducing the computational cost of optimizing agent prompts.

papers.title: What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: This paper presents a two-level framework that factorizes LLM agentic data and uses the Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) lens to guide constrained data generation.
key_points: Factorizes agentic data into a four-element tuple (E, q, tau, v) representing the environment specification, task signal, interaction realization, and optional verifier.
Formulates data generation as constrained distribution design evaluated through the Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity (ACE) lens.

Defines Accuracy as establishing grounded, internally consistent data support; Complexity as placing learning mass relative to a learner's capability; and Diversity as controlling coverage and redundancy.
Identifies a field-wide shift toward execution-grounded accuracy, learner-calibrated difficulty, and non-surface behavioral coverage.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized formal framework to evaluate and generate informative, non-redundant synthetic experience for evolving LLM agents instead of relying on raw dataset scaling.

papers.title: PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference

summary.tldr: PACE is a training-free VLM inference framework that uses a Condense-and-Extract paradigm to reduce computation in both the vision encoder and LLM.
key_points: Adaptive Pixel Compressor (APC) evaluates visual density before encoding to downsample redundant inputs and accelerate the vision encoder.
Dynamic Dual-Attention Extractor (DDAE) prunes visual tokens using fused internal visual encoder signals and LLM semantic signals.
Evaluating on Qwen2.5-VL-7B shows the model retains 93.8% of performance using 10% of visual tokens, achieving a 3.1x Time to First Token (TTFT) speedup.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly cuts VLM inference latency and computation without requiring model retraining or sacrificing critical fine-grained visual details.

papers.title: When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue

summary.tldr: Researchers created ContraTalk, a benchmark measuring cross-modal transcript bias in spoken dialogue, and introduced an Audio Twin framework to expose localized acoustic evidence directly to LLM reasoning models.
key_points: ContraTalk evaluates 501 questions across five discourse dimensions: interaction behavior, emotion state, dialogue act, social stance, and conversational intent.
Text-only LLMs reach over 90% accuracy on consistent transcript-audio cases but drop to 33-48% on cross-modal conflict cases.
Direct AudioLLMs select the transcript-biased incorrect option in roughly 30-40% of conflict cases.
The Audio Twin framework converts speech into a text-readable representation of localized acoustic cues, which reduces trap selection and improves conflict-case accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings show that current audio-language models rely heavily on text shortcuts, demonstrating the need for explicit acoustic evidence extraction to achieve reliable speech-grounded reasoning.

security.title: Perturbation Probing: A New Diagnostic for the Fragility of LLM Safety

summary.tldr: Unit 42 research introduces Perturbation Probing, revealing that LLM safety refusal mechanisms reside within a thin neural layer, demonstrating the inherent fragility of internal safety controls.
key_points: LLM safety refusal behaviors are localized within a thin neural layer.
Perturbation Probing acts as a new diagnostic tool to measure the fragility of AI safety mechanisms.
Internal model safety controls are fragile and require reinforcement.
summary.why_it_matters: Because internal safety mechanisms are localized and fragile, AI systems require external, multi-layered security controls to reliably prevent misuse.

security.title: Low-ASR Backdoors: Exploiting Attack Success Rate Reduction and Attacker-Defender Asymmetry

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce a reverse-training framework that deliberately lowers backdoor Attack Success Rates, demonstrating that state-of-the-art defenses fail when the attack success rate is artificially reduced.
key_points: Attack Success Rate (ASR) is demonstrated to be an attacker-controlled parameter rather than an intrinsic property of a backdoor.
A reverse-training framework is used to weaken the trigger-target association, creating low-ASR backdoors while retaining clean-input performance.
State-of-the-art backdoor defenses consistently fail when evaluated under low-ASR conditions across diverse architectures, datasets, and attack families.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes a critical flaw in current backdoor defense paradigms, which rely on high attack success rates to detect compromised models.

security.title: FIDA: Feature Instability-Driven Attack on Self-Supervised Facial Representation

summary.tldr: FIDA introduces a Feature Instability Loss objective for backdoor attacks on self-supervised face models, increasing triggered feature sensitivity to evade perturbation-based defenses while preserving benign utility.
key_points: Injects backdoors into self-supervised face representation models using subtle semantic triggers.
Introduces Feature Instability Loss, which trains encoders to increase sensitivity of triggered features along sampled perturbation directions.
Avoids rigid feature patterns typical of traditional backdoors to effectively bypass perturbation-based defense mechanisms.
Demonstrates high attack success rates and maintains benign utility across evaluated facial analysis settings.
summary.why_it_matters: FIDA reveals a critical security vulnerability in self-supervised facial analysis systems, showing that backdoor attacks can bypass state-of-the-art perturbation defenses.

security.title: Unsaid, Unsafe? Implicit Security Obligations in LLM-Based RTL Code Generation

summary.tldr: Researchers created SECRTL-GEN, a benchmark revealing severe security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated hardware, and introduced RTL-Obliger, a neuro-symbolic framework that infers implicit security obligations to generate safer RTL code.
key_points: SECRTL-GEN contains 392 tasks spanning five CWE families across four HDLs (Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL, and Python) with black-box functional and security testbenches.
Frontier LLMs under vanilla prompts achieve 73-79% functional pass rates but only 14-35% security pass rates, demonstrating that higher functional performance does not correlate with security.
RTL-Obliger extracts a functional-semantic graph from specifications, matches it against a CWE pattern ontology via a symbolic engine, and uses an LLM to generate functionality-preserving secure RTL.
RTL-Obliger increases mean all-pass rates to 61.6%, outperforming existing secure-generation baselines like SecV and RESCUE (49.6-51.4%).
summary.why_it_matters: Hardware security flaws in LLM-generated RTL cannot be patched after tape-out, making automated inference of implicit security requirements critical for safe silicon manufacturing.

security.title: How Do LLM Agents Actually Get the Flag? Trace-Level Provenance for Agentic Offensive Security Evaluation

summary.tldr: CTF-ABACUS is a trace-based auditing framework that reconstructs LLM agent runs into evidence-grounded solve profiles to verify if flags were obtained through true exploitation or shortcut pathways.
key_points: Evaluates agent runs by decomposing actions into penetration-testing phases and categorical techniques to detect flag exposure, memorized recall, external lookup, or guessing.
Generates challenge signatures by aggregating solve profiles across agents to reveal if benchmark challenges were solved via intended exploits versus shortcuts.
Audited 1,435 CTF attempts across 240 challenges using six frontier and open-source models, generating 2,870 solve profiles under two judge lenses.
Revealed that trace-verified exploits account for only 62-87% of recovered flags, with shortcut recoveries exhibiting substantially shallower execution trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts offensive AI security evaluations from binary flag counts to trace-verified execution, preventing the overestimation of autonomous agent cybersecurity capabilities.

security.title: MeMark: Membrane-Space Watermarking for Spiking Neural Networks

summary.tldr: MeMark is a membrane-space watermarking method for Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) that embeds multi-bit identifiers into the internal membrane states of Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons to survive output-head replacement.
key_points: Embeds secret bits directly into the internal membrane states of chosen Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons relative to their firing thresholds, eliminating the need for a learned decoder.
Tested on a 215.4M-parameter SpikeGPT checkpoint where all twenty 64-bit keys passed the 51/64 verification threshold, while 30,000 random keys produced zero false positives.
Maintains verifiable ownership evidence after fine-tuning, 90% parameter pruning, int8 quantization, and complete output-head replacement.
Evaluated across recurrent, convolutional, residual, and transformer SNN architectures against adaptive attacks, key disclosure, rollback, and student extraction.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust Intellectual Property (IP) verification and origin tracking for pretrained SNN checkpoints even when downstream users strip or replace the original output layer.

security.title: NeuronFuzz: Safety Neuron Guided Fuzzing for LLM Safety Evaluation

summary.tldr: NeuronFuzz is a white-box fuzzing framework that uses safety-neuron activations during prefill to provide continuous feedback, eliminating response generation from LLM safety evaluation.
key_points: Identifies a compact set of safety neurons via template-invariant inputs and stability-aware selection to compute a continuous safety alarm score.
Obtains execution feedback during the prefill stage, bypassing costly target-model response generation.
Uses gradients of the differentiable safety alarm score to locate safety-sensitive template positions for targeted masked language model mutations.
Achieves a 76-100% jailbreak discovery rate across five white-box models, outperforming baselines by up to 48 percentage points.
Transfers zero-shot to proprietary models, reaching an average Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 69.6% and top-5 Ensemble ASR (EASR) of 92.6%.
summary.why_it_matters: By relying on internal prefill activations instead of full generation loops, NeuronFuzz significantly reduces the computational cost of finding jailbreaks while improving attack transferability.

security.title: LAAF: A Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM Applications

summary.tldr: LAAF is an integrated layered accountability framework synthesized from a systematic review of 122 studies and 12 regulatory standards to trace, explain, and govern LLM application deployment.
key_points: Synthesizes evidence from 122 primary studies and 12 regulatory documents (2022–2026) using PRISMA methodology across five databases.

Structures accountability across four operational layers: provenance, application logic, human oversight, and governance and redress, intersected by traceability, role clarity, and continuous monitoring.
Maps accountability mechanisms directly to compliance frameworks including the EU AI Act high-risk obligations, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025).
Identifies key persistent gaps including under-specified human oversight, lack of shared accountability metrics, disciplinary silos, and insufficient empirical evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides organizations with a structured, multi-layered blueprint to operationalize AI governance and fulfill strict regulatory obligations like the EU AI Act across high-stakes domains.

summary.tldr: A systematic evaluation shows LLM-enhanced GNNs significantly increase vulnerability to link, label, and membership inference attacks compared to shallow text representation baselines due to semantic amplification in the embedding space.
key_points: Evaluated privacy risks across 42 victim model configurations combining LLM feature enhancers with GNN backbones across six text-attributed graph datasets.
Tested six privacy attack methods covering three specific threat vectors: link inference, label inference, and membership inference.
Discovered that LLM semantic enrichment amplifies privacy-sensitive signals within the embedding space, making models easier to exploit.
Evaluated differential privacy as a defense, finding it mitigates attack risks but causes severe utility degradation.
summary.why_it_matters: Deploying LLM-enhanced GNNs on private text-attributed graphs exposes sensitive structural, label, and membership data to inference attacks, and standard defenses like differential privacy significantly degrade model performance.

security.title: Adversarial Training of Linear Models under Stealthy Attacks

summary.tldr: A detector-based switched model framework for linear prediction models that uses a convex formulation of adversarial risk to guarantee robustness against stealthy false data injection attacks.
key_points: Introduces a detector-based switched model framework designed specifically to address optimal stealthy attack strategies.
Provides a convex formulation of the adversarial risk for linear prediction models.
Incorporates protected features and an attack probability hyperparameter to manage the trade-off between clean and adversarial data performance.
Demonstrates robust performance on real and synthetic datasets under partially attacked regimes, maintaining effectiveness even when attack probabilities are misspecified.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides theoretical guarantees and practical robustness for linear predictive models operating in environments subject to subtle, stealthy false data injection attacks.

security.title: SecureDrive-FL: Joint Differential Privacy and Gradient-Aware Selective Homomorphic Encryption for Federated Driver Monitoring

summary.tldr: SecureDrive-FL combines DP-SGD and GASHE, a dynamic threshold-based selective homomorphic encryption method, to secure federated driver monitoring against both model poisoning and Man-in-the-Middle gradient interception with 8-10% runtime overhead.
key_points: GASHE dynamically identifies and encrypts only the gradient components that exceed a DP-calibrated sensitivity threshold instead of using full-parameter CKKS or static layer-based encryption.
DP-SGD calibration parameters directly derive the GASHE encryption mask, establishing a unified pipeline for training-time privacy and communication-time confidentiality.
Under MitM attack scenarios, SecureDrive-FL maintains 78.2% accuracy while unencrypted DP-SGD degrades to 10.4% (near-random).

Against model poisoning, SecureDrive-FL matches DP-SGD performance (73.6% vs 74.0% accuracy, both yielding a 3.9% Attack Success Rate) under non-IID conditions with per-round privacy parameter epsilon_0=4.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that combining differential privacy with targeted homomorphic encryption can fully protect federated learning systems against transit interception without incurring the massive computational overhead typical of full-parameter encryption.

security.title: KubeCap: A Framework for Capability Minimization in Kubernetes via Static Analysis and LLM-Assisted Rule Inference

summary.tldr: KubeCap minimizes Kubernetes workload attack surfaces by combining static entrypoint reachability analysis with LLM-assisted kernel rule inference to automatically derive and configure minimal Linux capability sets in deployment manifests.
key_points: Empirical analysis of three open-source datasets revealed that 74.67% of Kubernetes projects lack explicit capability configurations.
KubeCap resolves deployment specs into deterministic manifests, identifies container entrypoints, and executes reachability-guided system call analysis.
The framework uses LLM-assisted rule specification on Linux kernel code to map syscall-parameter-capability relationships.
Evaluation on 10 Go-based Kubernetes projects achieved an average capability reduction rate of 54.97%, outperforming Rapid Type Analysis and Class Hierarchy Analysis baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables automated enforcement of the principle of least privilege in Kubernetes deployments without relying on manual security context configuration or runtime profiling.

security.title: Toward Interpretable Privacy Guarantees in Face-Swapping Anonymization

summary.tldr: A new linear stochastic model frames face-swapping algorithms as transformations on identity embeddings to explain and predict target identity leakage.
key_points: Empirical evaluations show face-swapping anonymization models suffer from persistent target identity leakage despite lower match scores.
The proposed linear stochastic model maps face-swapping operations directly within the identity embedding space.
The framework provides an interpretable account of privacy leakage mechanisms to derive and verify testable privacy predictions.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts facial anonymization evaluation from purely empirical observation to interpretable, mathematically grounded privacy guarantees.

security.title: Pointing the Way, Hiding the Destination: Practical Private Dense Retrieval at Scale

summary.tldr: A new private dense retrieval protocol uses learned deep hashing as a randomized filter to create short candidate lists, enabling efficient, accurate, and privacy-preserving RAG on large corpora.
key_points: Repurposes learned deep hashing to output randomized binary codes, selecting 200 to 500 candidate passages out of up to 5.4 million documents without sacrificing retrieval quality.
Combines candidate shortlisting with encrypted reranking and oblivious key transfer to protect user queries and selected documents while enforcing corpus access authorization.
Adds 0.73 seconds (a 10% overhead) to a 128-token Qwen3-32B RAG pipeline when evaluated on the 2.68 million-passage Natural Questions (NQ) corpus over a 10-Gbps network link.
Provides directional metric differential privacy (DP) and significantly mitigates embedding-inversion and property-inference attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that cryptographic search overhead can be drastically reduced to practical latency levels without degrading RAG zero-shot retrieval accuracy or exposing query privacy.

infra.title: vLLM Sessions at PyTorch Conference North America 2026

summary.tldr: PyTorch Conference NA 2026 will feature technical sessions on vLLM, highlighting native tiered KV cache offloading, disaggregated prefill/decode serving, and Elastic Expert Parallelism.
key_points: Native tiered KV cache offloading is integrated directly into vLLM, utilizing CPU memory as a universal transport hub to minimize GPU overhead without external dependencies.
Disaggregated serving features bidrectional KV transfer, a KV Push connector, and KV cache leases, which reduce time to first token and Pareto-dominate co-located serving on Nemotron.
Elastic Expert Parallelism allows vLLM runtime environments to dynamically add or remove workers and redistribute experts across available nodes.
A model-customized KV Cache Planner introduces model-specific planners to handle distinct KV cache requirements for architectures like MLA, SWA, Eagle, and DeepSeek-V4.
LMCache offers cluster-wide prompt caching across vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM, interfacing with backends like Mooncake, Redis, and AWS S3.
summary.why_it_matters: These architectural updates in vLLM enhance memory efficiency, lower latency, and enable dynamic scaling for high-throughput production LLM serving.

infra.title: Batch write and discover records in Amazon SageMaker Feature Store

summary.tldr: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store has launched the BatchWriteRecord and ListRecords APIs to enable multi-record batch ingestion and record enumeration across storage tiers.
key_points: BatchWriteRecord allows writing up to 25 records across multiple feature groups in a single API call with partial-success semantics and per-record TTL control.
BatchWriteRecord maintains EventTime-based ordering guarantees, writing newer records to the online store as the latest version and older ones as historical versions in the offline store.
ListRecords enables paginated enumeration of record identifiers within a feature group for both Standard (DynamoDB-backed) and In-Memory (Redis-backed) storage tiers.
Minimum IAM permissions for the new capabilities require actions for sagemaker:BatchWriteRecord, sagemaker:PutRecord, and sagemaker:ListRecords.
summary.why_it_matters: These APIs reduce API call overhead and tail latency for high-throughput feature ingestion pipelines while preventing unrecoverable data loss in In-Memory storage tiers.
